title: Staying with Adelaide Hall in London
summary: Adelaide Hall's big house, mostly closed up, in postwar London.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Oh yeah, sure! But Adelaide had this big house, and most of it was closed off, because there was no central heating. But she had a girl working for her, and she used to light the fire every evening. She'd set the burner that when I come in, so that I'd be warm at night. But in the daytime, man, I used to go outside to get warm. But you get used to it, you get around and you go to the different places. Of course, you know the first time I was there, I got over there just while they were still rationing, and there was no food. So we had a -- And I got over there at the time -- I think I was about the second, part of the second group that went over there. The first group that went over was Maurice Rocco and Pearl Bailey. Pearl went over with the Duke Ellington group. And we were all living in the same flat in '48.
